correctness.rationale: The three incident faces have intrinsic shortest paths equal to Euclidean straight segments; a shortest route to the opposite face crosses some edge, and unfolding gives the minimum of distances from three reflected vertex images. Their Voronoi cells partition the opposite equilateral face into three congruent centroidal triangles, giving unique farthest point G at 2/sqrt(3). Polar integration of the three incident wedges and three opposite Voronoi wedges yields disk area pi*r²/2 for r<=1 and 3[r²(pi/6-acos(1/r))+sqrt(r²-1)] for 1<r<2/sqrt(3); divide by surface area sqrt(3). Differentiation gives perimeter r*(pi-6acos(1/r)). Independent sympy Puiseux expansion proved disk-area defect -4sqrt(2)(r-1)^(3/2)+O((r-1)^(5/2)), and independent partitioned numerical polar integrations matched at eight radii (including both endpoints) to <1e-10. The auxiliary checks confirm, not replace, exact unfolding and integration.
residual_risks: Finite numerical calculations cannot replace exact infinite proof; conclusions rest on the reconstructed analytic argument and inspected source certificate.
Independent numerical quadrature needed piecewise partition at break radii; the correctly partitioned check passed to 1e-10.
